name: InnoCaption: Call Captioning
oneLine: US phone-call caption app with live stenographers or automatic captions, free through the FCC for eligible people with hearing loss.

platforms.detail: The app runs on iOS and Android phones and tablets. InnoCaption Web places captioned calls from a computer browser, or shows the phone's captions on a bigger screen.

deviceRequirements.detail: The help centre says iPhone XS or newer on iOS 15.1 or later, and Android 8.0 or later. It reports compatibility problems with Jitterbug and Motorola phones.

roomCaptions.detail: InnoCaption says its FCC-funded service can't be used when both people are in the same room, including a classroom. The same company has separate apps that aren't FCC-funded: InnoScribe (free, on Google Play) and Bridge Live (with the paid Bridge product).

groupConversations.detail: You can join conference call lines and add a third caller. InnoCaption Bot's meeting captions can be shared with other attendees by link; nothing is offered for groups in the same room.

languages.detail: AI captions can use a secondary language from a list of over 20, such as Spanish, Chinese, Vietnamese and Arabic. Live stenographers caption English only; the Security page still says AI supports Spanish in addition to English.

offline.detail: You need a mobile data or Wi-Fi connection to use InnoCaption.

speakerLabels.detail: InnoCaption Bot shows who is speaking in online meetings. On phone calls you can choose to caption only the other person, or your own voice too.

translation.detail: InnoCaption says captions match the language spoken on the call and it does not translate speech.

saveTranscripts.detail: Call transcripts are kept on your device and can be backed up to your own iCloud or Google account. Without a backup, deleting the app deletes them; they are not stored on InnoCaption's servers.

export.detail: Transcripts can be shared as .txt files or emailed, and a web Transcript Viewer turns a .txt file into a printable conversation.

fileUpload.detail: No InnoCaption page mentions transcribing an uploaded audio or video file.

summaries.detail: A Summarize button turns a saved call transcript into a summary with key points. The transcript goes to InnoCaption's server temporarily for this.

customWords.detail: You can add names, places and technical terms to a Custom Word List.

display.detail: You can change the caption background colour, font (Default, Serif or Dyslexic), size and bold text, and pinch to zoom during calls.

soundAlerts.detail: No alerts for sounds around you are described. Caption alert vibrates and flashes the screen when captions start again after a long hold.

phoneCalls.detail: InnoCaption captions incoming, outgoing and three-way calls, voicemail and 911 calls. It works with your existing number through call forwarding.

videoCalls.text: Meetings via web or Bot; no FaceTime
videoCalls.detail: InnoCaption Web captions meetings you dial into by phone, or sends InnoCaption Bot (AI captions only) to Teams, Meet, Zoom and Webex. The app can't caption FaceTime; a separate InnoCaption Video app makes captioned video calls.

mediaOnDevice.detail: No InnoCaption page describes captioning videos or other media playing on the device.

humanCaptioners.detail: You can switch between live stenographers (CART), available 24/7, and AI captions before or during a call. If every stenographer is busy, an optional AI fallback takes over.

privacy.text: Calls not kept; not used to train AI
privacy.detail: Transcripts stay on your device, and call audio and transcripts are not kept after the call, except voicemail. The privacy notice says your data is never used to train AI models; stenographers hear only the other person.

account.text: Yes; name, DOB, last 4 of SSN
account.detail: Registration asks for your full name, date of birth, last four digits of your SSN, home address and cell number, sent to the FCC's TRS Fund Administrator. You self-certify your hearing loss; no doctor's note is needed.

availability.detail: Only for eligible users based in the US with a US cell number, home address and SSN; US residents can keep using it on a trip abroad if they tell support first. The app was not found in the UK, Canada or Mexico App Stores.

freePlan.detail: Free for eligible US users with hearing loss or a speech disability, with no limit on the number or length of calls.

price.detail: The app is free with no in-app purchases on the App Store. Bridge, the company's separate workplace product, costs from US$300 per device plus US$80 a month (US prices, October 2026).

accessibilityFunding.text: Yes, FCC (IP CTS and IP Relay)
accessibilityFunding.detail: The FCC lists Mezmo Corporation (dba InnoCaption) with full IP CTS and conditional IP Relay certification. The service is paid from the federal TRS Fund.

strengths.text: It offers live human stenographers (CART) around the clock alongside AI captions, and you can switch during a call.
Free and unlimited for eligible US users, with no cap on the number or length of calls.
The privacy notice says call audio and transcripts are not kept after the call and your data is never used to train AI models.
Covers calls on phone, tablet and web browser, including 3-way calls, voicemail, 911 and online meetings through InnoCaption Bot.

limits.text: It can't be used for in-person conversations; InnoCaption says this is against the law for its FCC-funded service.
Only for eligible users in the US with a US cell number, residential address and SSN.
Stenographer captions are English only; other languages are AI-only, and nothing is translated.
It needs an internet connection; there is no offline mode.

sources.title: InnoCaption eligibility and why it's free
quotes: InnoCaption’s service is offered free of charge to eligible individuals who are deaf or hard of hearing and need captions to understand phone conversations.

sources.title: Usage limits for InnoCaption

sources.title: Languages available for captioning
quotes: InnoCaption is able to provide captioning in other languages using AI, so you can select a secondary language of your choice. You can choose from over 20 different languages, with more options being added to the app.

notes: InnoCaption is a brand of Mezmo Corporation (Irvine, CA), the App Store seller and Google Play developer. The FCC list shows Mezmo Corporation (dba InnoCaption) with full IP CTS certification, and also Mezmo Corporation (dba CaptionMate), a provider InnoCaption bought in 2024. Language claims conflict: the Security page says AI captions support Spanish in addition to English, while the help centre lists English + 28 secondary options and the Features page says many languages. InnoCaption calls itself the only call captioning app with stenographers; that is the company's own claim and was not checked independently. In-person captions: the InnoCaption app does not do it, but the same team offers InnoScribe (free, Android listing on Google Play, says it is not TRS-funded; no iOS listing found) and Bridge Live (comes with the paid Bridge workplace product from Mezmo Technologies Inc; the Bridge pricing page says 75+ languages, the Bridge Live App Store listing says 50+ online with English offline). These are separate products and are not counted in the facts above. The innocaption.com privacy policy page loads its text through a Termly embed that needs JavaScript; it was read in a browser (Termly policy viewer for UUID 9f39b78f-5477-42df-9d4f-565d4a79f313). The FCC IP CTS consumer guide returned 403 to WebFetch and was read in a browser instead; it describes communications assistants re-voicing captions and does not itself say the service is free. Cost and eligibility rules come from the FCC registration FAQ and InnoCaption's pages. The App Store lookup API returned no result for the UK, Canada and Mexico storefronts; other countries were not checked. /innocaption-bridge (linked from the homepage) returned 404.
